newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-HONG KONG MARCH TOWARDS CHINA SHOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-HONG KONG MARCH TOWARDS CHINA SHOWDOWN.

text.p: Hong Kong moved a step closer to a showdown with China following their 3-0 win against Italy in the women's team competition at the world table tennis championships on Friday.
The victory ensured Hong Kong a top three finish in their six-nation group and a place in the next stage of the competition.
Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule, have set their sights on bettering their bronze medal performances of 1989 and 1985.
Former Chinese internationals Chai Poh Wa and Chan Tan Luiot have led Hong Kong's climb to prominence and would dearly like a crack at defending champions China.
Chai crossed the border in 1986 two years ahead of Chan.
"They feel they are Hong Kong people after being here (in Hong Kong) so long," said women's team coach Cheung Yin.
"Playing against China has always been that little bit special for them and I suppose this championship has something extra about it."
Unbeaten China took the opportunity to rest world champion Deng Yaping and still had enough firepower to outclass Canada 3-0.
